gaps: No object gives the price reader the transport it calls. price_adapter_ycharts.py:94 calls transport(path, params) and expects the parsed JSON answer, but the stored session's request (operation_lease.py:242) takes a path that already carries its query string and returns a raw body (deadline_transport.py:85). A wrapper must build the query as runner.py:121 does, parse the body as generate/transport.py:288 does, and let errors propagate. The repo holds no such wrapper for fund_data.

The stored session is not passed into the pricing path. make_opal_stores (resident_installed.py:536) and _pricing_extras (resident_installed.py:373) take no session, so the cell must thread the session from resident_installed.py:527. The lease is reachable from the producer's process: the stores closure is called in-process per job (resident_worker.py:534), so no out-of-process lease path was found.

No window or count budget bounds the price stage. opal_producer.py:282 and :295 issue one reader call per unique holding plus two calls for SPY and BIL, in one run, and runner.py:41 records that the 7th request of a lease window is challenged. The binding validator (resident_installed.py:115-124) checks only enabled and tiers, so no ycharts budget exists yet.

The YCharts security id form for a plain holding ticker is not established. price_adapter_ycharts.py:94 sends id:<TICKER>. The repo's only served id forms are the portfolio security_id placeholder and the benchmark id:^SPXTR, both in the pinned overview map, which is readable only at HEAD (see the next gap). No repo evidence shows that id:<TICKER> resolves at YCharts.

The pinned overview map (build_resident_package.py:45) is absent from this sparse worktree: the sparse checkout includes only org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_ANLREQ under the IRPT folder. The file was read only through git show of HEAD (blob da312a9b), so no line of it is cited here. At HEAD the file has no expand key, so its holdings-expansion spec is not a source of the ticker template.

The served shape of a single-ticker fund_data answer at zoom max is not measured by any live capture identified in the repo. The shape is evidenced only by the adapter's docstring, its test fixtures and kept fixture files (for example ycharts/research/tests/fixtures/kept/step=01_fixture_series.json).

Whether the price route answers a signed-out caller is not established. The sessionless transport (resident_session.py:120) is documented only for the signed-out ticker lookup, so the cell is expected to use the session-bearing acquire (resident_session.py:115), and no live check of that choice is in the repo.
